# Cloud Modular: full information

> Cloud Modular delivers architecturally designed modular buildings, certified to Australian Standards, for faster delivery and greater certainty.

Website: https://cloudmodular.com.au

## Company

Cloud Modular designs and delivers modular buildings for developers, builders and government clients. We are based in Karrinyup, Perth, Western Australia, and deliver nationally, with no minimum project size.

Modules are built in our manufacturing facility in Foshan, China, with the structure, services and fit-out built in. Each module is inspected before it leaves the factory, then shipped to the nearest suitable port, cleared through customs and biosecurity, transported by road and craned onto footings prepared on site. Because the site works and the factory production run at the same time, the overall programme is shorter than building everything on site.

Our production capability gives us access to more than 450,000 square metres of dedicated manufacturing facilities, with the systems, supply chain and capacity for repeatable modular delivery. That capability has delivered projects from design to installation in Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Melbourne, Saipan and Auckland, and we now bring it to Western Australia.

## Why now

Australia's population is projected to grow by 2.18 million people in the five years to 2026–27, an average of 435,200 people a year. At the same time, insolvencies across the construction sector have reduced the number of builders available to meet demand.

## Sectors

- Commercial: offices, retail and mixed-use developments
- Multi-residential: apartments, townhouses and residential developments
- Health and aged care: medical facilities and aged care residences
- Education and community: schools, libraries and community centres
- Infrastructure: transit facilities and public infrastructure
- Hotels and accommodation: hotels, resorts and short-stay accommodation

## Ways to work with us

- Design and deliver. We take the project from feasibility to handover as one team, leading the design, manufacture, shipping and installation, and appointing and managing the architect, engineer, building surveyor and builder.
- Early involvement. We join your architect and consultants at feasibility so the design suits manufacture before it is fixed, then supply the modules or deliver the whole project.
- Supply to your builder. We resolve the design for manufacture with your team, then build, inspect, ship and deliver the modules. Your builder holds the building permit and looks after the site works, footings, services and connections.
- Tender response. We price tender documents for modular construction and show where design changes could save time or cost.

## Process

1. Brief and feasibility: site, brief and budget; yield and programme tested; modular fit confirmed.
2. Design for manufacture: the design is resolved around module sizes, transport limits and crane lifts; the structure is designed for the site's wind region, including cyclone regions.
3. Approvals and documentation: planning and building approval documents; the registered builder lodges the building permit; shop drawings are produced for the factory.
4. Manufacture in Foshan: modules are built with structure, services and fit-out while the site is prepared.
5. Inspection and sign-off: independent inspections at key stages; engineering sign-off and import documents completed before anything leaves the factory.
6. Shipping and clearance: shipped, then cleared through customs and biosecurity; road transport planned to site, including regional and remote locations.
7. Delivery and installation: modules arrive in an agreed sequence, are craned onto prepared footings, then joined, sealed and connected to services.
8. Completion and handover: the builder completes finishing works, the building surveyor carries out the final inspection, and keys, manuals and warranties are handed over.

## Manufacturing and quality

Checks run at key stages of design, production and the lead-up to installation. In the factory, every module passes a series of inspections before it moves to the next stage, and each check is recorded with photographs against the module's number. The full record is handed over with the building. Checks cover materials on arrival, asbestos-free materials, the frame and welding, services before the linings close, the envelope and waterproofing, and a final inspection before shipping.

Typical build-ups include light-gauge steel stud walls with rock wool insulation, fire-rated plasterboard and a vapour barrier inside, and fibre cement board, a breathable membrane, battens and cladding outside.

## Certification

Modules are designed and documented to the National Construction Code, and each building is certified in Western Australia in the same way as any other. The building surveyor reviews the design before production starts, and the builder holds the building permit.

- Structural design: the engineer designs the structure for the building class, loads and wind region, including module frames, connections between modules and hold-down to footings, and certifies the structure as built.
- Cyclone wind regions: in regions C and D the structure, cladding, windows and connections are designed for the wind loads in AS/NZS 1170.2.
- Imported products: glazing meets the Australian glass and window standards, electrical products carry the RCM mark, and plumbing products are WaterMark certified.
- Fire safety: walls and ceilings use non-combustible rock wool insulation and fire-rated plasterboard; the building surveyor checks tested systems meet any required fire-resistance level.
- Energy efficiency: each design is assessed under the National Construction Code.
- Warranties: the warranties required in Western Australia, including the builder's statutory obligations and home indemnity insurance for residential work, plus a warranty on the structure and workmanship of the modules and each product's manufacturer warranty.

## Projects

All projects are in progress.

### Seashells Jurien Bay (Jurien Bay, WA)

A beachfront resort community of 108 residences on Western Australia's Turquoise Coast, about two hours north of Perth, developed by MVP Group and manufactured by Cloud Modular. The residences are designed for an 8-star energy rating, with double glazing, solar generation, battery storage and EV charging. Residence types: the 4 Bed Bay View Villa, the 4 Bed Hasting Street Villa, a three-bedroom detached villa and a two-bedroom detached villa.
https://cloudmodular.com.au/our-work/seashells-jurien-bay/

### Capel Village (Capel, WA)

An approved over-55s lifestyle village of 52 single-storey residences at 96 Capel Drive in Western Australia's South West, developed by MVP Group and manufactured by Cloud Modular. The masterplan keeps the mature marri and jarrah canopy. The village received regional development assessment panel approval on 5 March 2026.
https://cloudmodular.com.au/our-work/capel-village/

### 25 On Rowland and Forrest (Subiaco, WA)

A mixed-use building of 18 modular apartments on a corner site in central Subiaco, designed by Doepel Marsh Architects and manufactured by Cloud Modular. The apartment modules are made while the basement and ground floor are built on site, then craned into place above them. Most apartments have one bedroom and a balcony, and the top floors hold two-level loft apartments with their own decks.
https://cloudmodular.com.au/our-work/25-on-rowland-and-forrest/

## Frequently asked questions

Where are the modules built?
In our manufacturing facility in Foshan, China. Every module is inspected at each stage of production and signed off before it is packed and shipped to site.

How do the modules comply with Australian standards?
They are designed and documented to the National Construction Code and certified in Western Australia like any other building. Full documentation and drawings are provided for building surveyors and local authorities.

Can modular buildings be customised?
Yes. Modules are designed to suit site constraints, planning requirements and spatial needs.

How are modules transported and installed?
They are shipped, unloaded and craned into position. We coordinate with local contractors for footings, services and final works.

Do modular buildings last as long as traditional buildings?
Yes. Modules are engineered as permanent structures and use materials and systems comparable to traditional builds.

What is the typical timeline?
It depends on scale and complexity, but factory production and site works run at the same time, which shortens the overall programme.
